 Conservative YouTuber and comedian Alex Stein visited the University Union Amphitheater with NAU’s Turning Point USA (TPUSA) chapter to debate students about transgender athletes, government transparency and other worldwide issues on Nov. 3.
 Stein began debating students at different college institutions in September 2024. His presence as a debater expanded after Charlie Kirk’s assassination, when he took over TPUSA’s on-campus “ Pick Up the Mic ” events.
 Throughout the debate, Stein touched on Proposition 318 , which was featured in Coconino County’s midterm ballots and passed on Election Day. 
 The proposition requires schools and athletic associations to restrict sports participation and access to private spaces, like locker rooms and bathrooms, based on each athlete’s biological sex at birth.
 Stein said he has “different” beliefs about transgender individuals in women's sports, and that he enjoys placing sports bets on them.
 “I like transgenders in women’s sports because I like to gamble on them, and I want to win money,” Stein said. “I think transgenders have an advantage in women’s sports.”
 Stein said he recently won money on his last DraftKings bet involving American swimmer Lia Thomas .
 He also expressed skepticism toward the U.S. government, particularly about transparency and the information it shares with the public.
 Freshman Kamya McNeal speaks to Turning Point USA debater Alex Stein at the "Pick Up the Mic" event at the University Union Amphitheater on Nov. 3. Alyssa Estrada/The Lumberjack 
 During the COVID-19 pandemic, he said he believed the federal government   lied to the people about how vaccines were going to prevent transmission and infection.
 Stein added that he wants more U.S. government transparency no matter who is in office, whether they are a Democrat or Republican. He said it is not always the government’s best interest to tell the country the truth.
 “Once you start trading any amount of freedom for safety, you end up with no freedom or no safety,” Stein said.
 Midway through the debate, NAUPD arrested a student for engaging in disorderly conduct and trespassing. According to the police report, the student was singing loudly and moving closer to Stein during his event.
 Attendees complained about the student to NAUPD officers, leading to their arrest.
 Students for a Democratic Society  began protesting after the student was arrested. The club members chanted “No ICE, no KKK and no fascist USA” and “F- your system, f- your hate. We are not here for debate.”
 Several other college students have been arrested while protesting Stein. During an Oct. 28 debate at the University of Oregon , local law enforcement officers arrested  three student protesters for disorderly conduct and harassment.
 Bugga Baylish, an NAU freshman studying engineering, spoke to Stein during the event about his thoughts regarding recent Native American deportations .
 Baylish asked Stein if he was aware of the recent deportations, but Stein said he was confused and was unaware of them. 
 NAUPD talks to Students for a Democratic Society students near the University Union Amphitheater during a “Pick up the Mic Initiative" event, Nov. 3. Elliott Stringer/The Lumberjack 
 He added that he felt disrespected by Stein when speaking about his personal experiences as a Native American. 
 “To be honest, it kind of confused me,” Baylish said. “It made me feel kind of a little bit disrespected. His responses were just kind of weird to me because they didn’t really make sense.”
 Baylish said Stein’s responses typically did not answer the questions he asked.
 Instead, he said the debaters’ answers were confusing and often led in multiple different directions.
 “He also mentioned that he was Native American,” Baylish said. “I don’t know, it just kind of feels odd to me because I feel like a lot of people say they’re Native American, but they’re that really small percentage.”
 Baylish said he did not think Stein’s visit significantly impacted students on campus, but acknowledged that its timing during the midterm elections could have drawn interest.
 For more information regarding TPUSA, visit the organization’s Instagram account. More information on Stein and his upcoming events can be found on his website.
